correctness.rationale: After centering K, central symmetry gives f(-y)=g(y) and an even chord-length function. The exact source definition makes the transformed fiber [-lambda*l(y),(1-lambda)*l(y)]. If the transformed body is centrally symmetric, its center projects to the unique center of the projected body, so comparison of opposite fibers gives 2t=(1-2lambda)l(y). For lambda<1/2 the chord length is constant. Since f and g are convex and f+g is constant, f and g are affine, yielding K=F+[0,L]u. The converse is immediate. Each such direction determines a unique translated facet pair; convex bodies have at most countably many facets because their boundary has finite surface measure. Affine equivalence preserves central symmetry, so lambda-invariance would require uncountably many such directions, a contradiction.

value.rationale: Conjecture 7.2 is the source's main stated higher-dimensional invariant-body problem. The theorem removes the entire centrally symmetric class for every intermediate parameter, including the most natural ellipsoidal and strictly convex symmetric candidates. It also gives a reusable one-step structural criterion: preservation of central symmetry occurs exactly in prism directions, and there are only countably many of them. This is a motivated structural advance rather than an arbitrary special case.
